cohort: The study included 31,419 Cesarean deliveries performed at a single tertiary university-affiliated medical center between January 2011 and April 2022.
finding: The use of absorbable subcutaneous staples for skin closure during Cesarean delivery was associated with significantly shorter surgery times and a lower risk of prolonged hospitalization and readmission within 45 days.
mod_finding: The use of absorbable subcutaneous staples for skin closure during Cesarean delivery was associated with shorter surgery times and reduced risks of prolonged hospitalization and readmission compared to non-absorbable staples and sutures.
